description: North Dakota-only rules checked against the cited Century Code. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines.

questions.q: North Dakota's presumably lawful speed when passing a school during recess, or while children are going to or leaving during opening or closing hours, is
questions.explanation: Section 39-09-02(1)(b) of the North Dakota Century Code sets twenty miles an hour when passing a school during school recess or while children are going to or leaving school during opening or closing hours, unless a lower speed is designated or posted by local authorities. These figures are presumably lawful speeds under the basic rule in 39-09-01.

questions.q: On a North Dakota highway in a business district, residence district, or public park, the presumably lawful speed is
questions.explanation: Section 39-09-02(1)(e) sets twenty-five miles an hour on any highway in a business district, a residence district, or a public park, unless a different speed is designated and posted by local authorities.

questions.q: North Dakota's presumably lawful speed on an access-controlled, paved and divided, multilane interstate is
questions.explanation: Section 39-09-02(1)(i) sets eighty miles an hour on access-controlled, paved and divided, multilane interstate highways, unless otherwise permitted, restricted, or required by conditions. Paragraph (h) separately sets seventy miles an hour on other paved and divided multilane highways.

questions.q: On a paved two-lane North Dakota county or township highway with no speed posted, the presumably lawful speed is 55 mph. A 65 mph two-lane limit applies
questions.explanation: Section 39-09-02(1)(f) sets fifty-five miles an hour on gravel, dirt, or loose-surface highways and on paved two-lane county and township highways if there is no speed limit posted. Paragraph (g) sets sixty-five miles an hour on paved two-lane highways if posted for that speed.

questions.q: North Dakota's criminal DUI alcohol concentration is
questions.explanation: Section 39-08-01(1)(a)(1) prohibits driving or actual physical control if the person has an alcohol concentration of at least eight one-hundredths of one percent by weight at the time of a chemical test within two hours after the driving or physical control.

questions.q: A person who drives a commercial motor vehicle in North Dakota with an alcohol concentration of at least four one-hundredths
options: is within the legal commercial limit
must be disqualified from driving a commercial vehicle
is held to eight one-hundredths, the same as a car
questions.explanation: Section 39-06.2-10.1 says any person who drives or is in actual physical control of a commercial motor vehicle with an alcohol concentration of at least four one-hundredths of one percent by weight must, in addition to any other sanctions, be disqualified from driving a commercial motor vehicle under section 39-06.2-10.

questions.q: North Dakota suspends an operator's license when the accumulated point total is
options: A total of 12 or more points
questions.explanation: Section 39-06.1-10 says that if the driving record shows an accumulated total of twelve or more points, the director notifies the licensee of an intention to suspend. After hearing or opportunity for hearing, twelve points means a 7-day suspension, and thirteen and above means 7 days for each point over eleven. The section does not say the 12 points must be accumulated within 12 months.

questions.q: On a North Dakota road that is not covered by the higher posted-speed scale, speeding points start at
questions.explanation: Section 39-06.1-10(3)(a)(30), which applies except as provided in paragraph 33, assigns 0 points for 6 to 10 mph over the limit, 1 point for 11 to 15, 3 points for 16 to 20, 5 for 21 to 25, 9 for 26 to 35, 12 for 36 to 45, and 15 for 46 or more.

questions.q: If the posted speed limit is over 65 mph, North Dakota's speeding-point scale assigns
options: the same points as every other road
questions.explanation: Section 39-06.1-10(3)(a)(33) applies on a highway posted in excess of sixty-five miles an hour. That scale is 0 points for 1 to 5 mph over, 1 point for 6 to 10, 3 for 11 to 15, 5 for 16 to 20, 7 for 21 to 25, 10 for 26 to 30, 12 for 31 to 35, and 15 for 36 or more.

questions.q: North Dakota reduces the point total by
questions.explanation: Section 39-06.1-13(1) requires the director to reduce the point total by one point for each three-month period during which points are not recorded for a moving violation or for a violation listed in paragraphs 12 through 16 of 39-06.1-10(3)(a). The period is calculated from the date the last points were entered.

questions.q: A North Dakota class D instruction permit may be issued at 14. While using it, the driver must be accompanied by someone who
options: is a parent riding anywhere in the car
is at least 21 with 1 year of experience
is any licensed driver 16 or older
questions.explanation: Section 39-06-04 allows a resident at least fourteen to apply for a class D instruction permit. Subsection 3 requires accompaniment by a person with a class A, B, C, or D license, at least eighteen, with at least three years of driving experience, occupying a seat beside the driver.

questions.q: A North Dakotan who is not yet 18 is not eligible for a class D license until an instruction permit has been held for
questions.explanation: Section 39-06-04(4) says an individual who is not yet eighteen is not eligible for a class D license until an instruction permit has been issued for at least six months, or at least twelve months if the individual is under sixteen. The director may count a permit from another jurisdiction.

questions.q: A restricted North Dakota class D license for a minor to drive a listed family vehicle requires the minor to be at least 15 and to have
questions.explanation: Section 39-06-17(2) allows a restricted class D license at fifteen or older to operate the parent's, guardian's, grandparent's, sibling's, aunt's, or uncle's automobile when the listed conditions are met, including an approved driver-education or commercial course and a minimum of fifty hours of supervised behind-the-wheel experience in those conditions.

questions.q: A minor with that restricted North Dakota class D license may not drive
options: between the later of sunset or 9 p.m. and 5 a.m.
between midnight and 5 a.m. with no exceptions
questions.explanation: Section 39-06-17(4)(d) sets that night restriction for a restricted class D license issued under subsection 2. Subsection 4(b) limits passengers only to the manufacturer's suggested capacity. It is not a separate ban on teenage passengers. The night rule is for this restricted license, not a curfew written onto every class D license. Between the later of sunset or 9 p.m. and 5 a.m., unless a parent, guardian, or person 18 or older is in the front seat, or the trip is directly to or from work, an official school activity, or a religious activity.

questions.q: In North Dakota, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: North Dakota issues a learner's permit for a car at 14 years at the earliest.
questions.remember: North Dakota car permit: 14 years at the earliest.

provenance.manual: How to Apply for a Learner's Permit | NDDOT

questions.q: In North Dakota, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: North Dakota requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 6 months.
questions.remember: North Dakota: hold the permit 6 months.

provenance.manual: How to Apply for a Learner's Permit | NDDOT

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in North Dakota complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: North Dakota requires 50 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.
questions.remember: North Dakota: 50 hours of supervised driving.

provenance.manual: How to Apply for a Learner's Permit | NDDOT

questions.q: In North Dakota, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In North Dakota, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 15 years.
questions.remember: North Dakota: driving alone from 15 years.

questions.q: During which hours may a newly licensed teen in North Dakota not drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: North Dakota restricts provisional drivers from 9 p.m. to 5 a.m., with exceptions such as work or school.
questions.remember: North Dakota new drivers: off the road 9 p.m. to 5 a.m..

provenance.manual: How to Apply for a Learner's Permit | NDDOT

questions.q: In North Dakota, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: North Dakota drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 16 years.

questions.q: In North Dakota, a driver under 21 breaks the law at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: North Dakota sets the under-21 limit at 0.02%.

provenance.manual: NDHP Frequently Asked Questions | North Dakota State Highway Patrol

questions.q: In North Dakota, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in North Dakota brings a suspension of 180 days.
questions.remember: North Dakota, first refusal: 180 days without a license.

provenance.manual: Penalties for Driving Under the Influence | NDDOT

questions.q: Unless a sign says otherwise, what is the speed limit in a North Dakota residential district?
questions.explanation: North Dakota sets 25 mph in residential districts unless another limit is posted.

provenance.manual: North Dakota Century Code Chapter 39-09 Speed Limitations

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in North Dakota?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in North Dakota can be posted up to 80 mph for cars.
questions.remember: North Dakota rural interstate: up to 80 mph.

provenance.manual: NDHP Frequently Asked Questions | North Dakota State Highway Patrol

questions.q: Which best describes North Dakota's law on drivers using a phone?
options: No statewide ban on phone use or texting
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
Only texting is banned for all drivers
Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
questions.explanation: North Dakota: only texting is banned for all drivers.
questions.remember: North Dakota phone law: no texting.

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in North Dakota?
options: From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In North Dakota, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.
questions.remember: North Dakota left on red: one-way onto one-way only.

questions.q: How is North Dakota's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
No seat belt law for adults
Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
questions.explanation: North Dakota seat belt enforcement is primary.
questions.remember: North Dakota seat belts: primary law.

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in North Dakota?
questions.explanation: North Dakota requires a car seat or booster until 8 years, with height or weight exceptions.
questions.remember: North Dakota: car or booster seat until 8 years.

questions.q: What is North Dakota's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: North Dakota requires at least $25,000 / $50,000 / $25,000.
